title: Implement Function from Spec
description: Generate a single, well-tested function from a precise specification.
content:
Implement a {{language}} function named `{{name}}` that satisfies this specification:

{{spec}}

Requirements:
- Handle all edge cases explicitly (empty input, nulls, boundaries, overflow).
- No external dependencies unless I name them.
- Add a short docstring describing parameters, return value, and thrown errors.
- Follow idiomatic style and naming for {{language}}.

After the implementation, list the edge cases you handled and any assumptions you made.

title: Add Feature to Existing Code
description: Extend a codebase with a new feature while preserving existing behavior and conventions.
content:
I want to add the following feature: {{feature}}

Before writing code:
1. Identify the files and functions that must change, and explain why.
2. Describe how you'll keep existing behavior intact (and which tests prove it).
3. Match the project's existing patterns, naming, and error-handling style.

Then implement the change as a minimal, reviewable diff. Call out any place where the existing code made you choose between two reasonable approaches.

title: Explain This Code
description: Get a clear, layered explanation of an unfamiliar piece of code.
content:
Explain the following code:

```
{{code}}
```

Structure your answer as:
1. One sentence: what it does overall.
2. A step-by-step walk-through of the control flow.
3. Any non-obvious details — performance characteristics, side effects, edge cases, or subtle bugs.
4. What a caller needs to know to use it correctly.

Assume I'm a competent engineer new to this specific code.

title: Convert Pseudocode to Code
description: Translate an algorithm or pseudocode into working, idiomatic code.
content:
Translate the following pseudocode/algorithm into idiomatic {{language}}:

{{pseudocode}}

- Preserve the algorithm's complexity; note the Big-O of the result.
- Use clear names; don't leave single-letter variables unless conventional.
- Add input validation where a real caller could pass bad data.
- Include a couple of usage examples.

title: Implement an API Client
description: Write a typed client for a REST or RPC API from its docs.
content:
Write a {{language}} client for this API:

{{api_description}}

Requirements:
- Strong types for every request and response shape.
- Centralized error handling that distinguishes network, 4xx, and 5xx failures.
- Timeouts and a single, configurable retry policy for idempotent calls.
- No secrets in code — read credentials from configuration/env.
- A short usage example for the two most common calls.

title: Add Robust Error Handling
description: Harden a function or module against failure with deliberate error handling.
content:
Review the code below and add robust error handling:

```
{{code}}
```

For each failure mode, decide deliberately: validate-and-reject, retry, fall back, or propagate. Then:
- Validate inputs at the boundary; fail fast with actionable messages.
- Never swallow errors silently — log or rethrow with context.
- Distinguish expected failures (return/throw typed errors) from bugs (let them surface).
- Keep the happy path readable; don't drown it in try/catch.

Show the revised code and a one-line rationale per change.

title: Write a CLI Command
description: Build a command-line subcommand with argument parsing and good UX.
content:
Create a CLI command `{{command}}` in {{language}} that: {{behavior}}

Requirements:
- Parse flags and positional args with clear `--help` output.
- Validate arguments and exit with a non-zero code and a useful message on error.
- Support `--json` for machine-readable output where it makes sense.
- Be quiet on success by default; add `--verbose` for detail.
- Handle Ctrl+C cleanly.

title: Concurrency-Safe Implementation
description: Implement logic that is correct under concurrent access.
content:
Implement the following with correct behavior under concurrency: {{task}}

In {{language}}:
- Identify the shared state and the exact invariants that must hold.
- Choose the simplest correct synchronization (immutability > message passing > locks).
- Avoid deadlocks and races; explain why your choice is free of both.
- Note the performance trade-off you made.

Provide the code plus a short paragraph on how it behaves under contention.

title: Design a Regular Expression
description: Build and explain a regex for a specific matching task.
content:
Write a regular expression that matches: {{requirement}}

Provide the pattern in {{flavor}} syntax, a plain-language breakdown of each part, 3 strings it SHOULD match and 3 it should NOT, and a note on any catastrophic-backtracking risk and how to avoid it. Prefer readability (named groups) over cleverness.

title: Choose a Data Structure
description: Pick the right data structure for an access pattern.
content:
I need to store and access data like this: {{access_pattern}}

Recommend the data structure. Compare the 2-3 viable candidates on the operations I care about (insert, lookup, delete, iterate, ordered) with their Big-O. State the memory trade-off and which one wins for MY pattern. Flag the structure people reach for by habit that would be wrong here.

variables.name: access_pattern
variables.description: How the data is written and read

title: Implement a State Machine
description: Model a process as an explicit finite state machine.
content:
Model this as a state machine: {{process}}

Define the states, the events/transitions between them, and the actions on each transition. Make illegal transitions impossible to represent. Implement it in {{language}} with a clear transition table or typed states. Call out the states that are easy to forget: error, timeout, cancelled.

title: Add a Caching Layer
description: Introduce caching to a hot path correctly.
content:
I want to cache: {{what}}

Design the cache: the key, what to store, the eviction policy, and the TTL. Critically, define the INVALIDATION strategy: when does cached data go stale and how is it refreshed? Handle the cache-stampede and stale-read cases. Tell me how I will measure hit rate and whether this cache is even worth it.

title: Optimize a Hot Path
description: Make a performance-critical piece of code faster.

title: Implement Pagination
description: Add correct pagination to a list endpoint or query.
content:
I need to paginate: {{what}}

Recommend cursor-based or offset-based for my case and say why. Show the implementation: the page size, how the cursor or offset is encoded, how the client asks for the next page, and how the last page is detected. Handle the edge cases: items inserted or deleted mid-iteration, an invalid cursor, and an empty result. Note the stability and performance trade-off of the choice.

title: Write a Parser
description: Parse a structured text format into a usable structure.
content:
Write a parser for this format: {{format}}

Define the grammar or structure first, then implement it in {{language}}. Decide between a hand-written recursive-descent parser and a regex/split approach, and justify it. Produce clear errors with position info on malformed input rather than silently misparsing. Cover the tricky cases: nesting, escaping, whitespace, and empty input. Include a couple of example inputs and their parsed output.

title: Validate Untrusted Input
description: Validate and sanitize input at a trust boundary.
content:
This input crosses a trust boundary: {{input}}

Write validation that rejects anything that isn't explicitly allowed (allow-list, not deny-list). Define the shape, types, ranges, and formats that are valid, and the exact error for each violation. Normalize before comparing. Cover the attack-shaped cases: oversized, malformed, injection, and unexpected encodings. Tell me what to do on failure (reject vs coerce) and why reject is usually right here.

title: Proof-Driven Type & Boundary Guard
description: Autonomously find one unsafe type cast or unvalidated runtime boundary per round, prove how malformed data corrupts state or crashes downstream, and replace it with a verified type guard.
content:
# ROLE: Autonomous Proof-Driven Type & Boundary Guard

Act as a principal TypeScript and API contract engineer specializing in sound type narrowing, runtime schema validation at trust boundaries, discriminated unions, and invariant preservation. Work on exactly one concrete type-safety hole or unvalidated boundary (`as any`, `as unknown as T`, `@ts-expect-error`, non-null `!` assertion on external data, or unvalidated `JSON.parse` / IPC / storage / network payload) in this round when you can prove that a realistic malformed or edge-case input crosses that hole and causes a downstream crash, silent state corruption, or contract violation.

## Non-negotiable rules

- Runtime failure proof before fix: do not replace type casts purely for cosmetics. Prove with a runnable test that an unvalidated or malformed value passes through the current unsafe cast/boundary and causes a real failure or corrupted state downstream.
- One boundary per round: do not perform sweeping multi-file type cleanups in a single round.
- True narrowing over new casts: replace the unsafe cast with a sound runtime type guard, schema check, or discriminated union check. Never trade `as any` for `as unknown as T` or a looser type that hides the problem.
- Preserve valid caller contracts: include a control case proving that all valid inputs continue to behave identically.
- Shared checkout discipline: inspect repository instructions and working-tree state first. Preserve unrelated user or concurrent changes.
- Pre-flight toolchain & version verification: inspect repository manifests (`package.json`, `bun.lock`, `.bun-version`, `tsconfig.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `go.mod`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`) first to identify the target project's actual language, runtime, exact installed versions, runner commands (for example `cargo test`/`cargo clippy`, `pytest`/`ruff`/`mypy`, `go test`, or in Bun/Vitest repos `bun run test` rather than `bun test`, `bun run lint`, and the authoritative compiler/typechecker), and pinned constraints. Never rely on memorized or outdated APIs; verify current framework/library semantics against the repo's installed version and `packages/core/skills/tech-stack/references/current-versions.md` or live registries before authoring proofs, schemas, or fixes.
- No proof theatre: a setup/import failure, missing dependency, or timeout is blocked verification, not proof.
- Solo execution: do not spawn or delegate to other agents during the round.
- Evidence continuity: before each new round, read the prior round reports and do not repeat a boundary already hardened.

## Required skills (load before step 1)

<!-- wrongstack:required-skills typescript-strict api-design testing verify-before-done -->
Before any discovery, load each of these skills with the `skill` tool, including any continuation pages: $typescript-strict, $api-design, $testing, $verify-before-done. They are the working playbook for this protocol: typescript-strict for sound narrowing and eliminating unsafe assertions, api-design for boundary contract semantics and error shapes, testing for the proof and permanent regression test, and verify-before-done for the final verification gate and report. Where a skill's default behavior conflicts with this prompt, this prompt wins. If a skill is unavailable or fails to load, say so before starting and in the round report, then continue with this protocol without inventing that skill's contents. At the start of each later round, reload any required skill whose full text is no longer in your context, for example after compaction. The host enforces this: until each skill has been loaded to its last page or reported unavailable by the `skill` tool, every file-changing or command-running tool is refused; reading and searching still work.

## Round protocol

### 1. Discover unsafe casts and unvalidated boundaries
Record the starting revision, dirty paths, and target scope. Search the target scope for `as any`, `as unknown as`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `JSON.parse`, unchecked index access, or external payload handlers (WebSocket frames, persisted JSON files, CLI flags, environment/config loaders, MCP/tool arguments). Use `codebase-incoming-calls` and `codebase-invariant-check` to see how callers supply data and what invariants downstream consumers assume. Select one boundary where malformed input can realistically reach production code and cause damage.

### 2. Prove the unfixed boundary hole
Create a round-owned workspace under `.temp_files/proof-driven-type-boundary-guard/<round-id>/`. Choose a collision-free round-id for this run. The proof must:

1. call the real production boundary with a malformed, partial, wrong-primitive, or nullish runtime value that the TypeScript compiler currently ignores because of the unsafe cast or `any`;
2. include a valid-input control case;
3. assert the expected safe behavior (deterministic validation error, safe fallback, or rejected input instead of an unhandled `TypeError`, `NaN` propagation, or silent state corruption downstream);
4. exit non-zero and print an explicit `FAIL` reason against the unfixed code.

Run the proof before editing production code and retain the exact command, working directory, exit code, and failure output. Confirm whether the runner loads source or built output; rebuild the affected dependency chain if needed so both runs exercise the intended revision. If you cannot produce a failing proof, do not modify production code; report `no-proven-bug`.

### 3. Apply the surgical type & runtime guard
Replace the unsafe cast with a precise type predicate, runtime shape validator, or exhaustive narrowing check, and ensure `typecheck` (including `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` / `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` where enabled) passes cleanly without suppression comments.

### 4. Verify and clean up
Re-run the same proof with the same assertions and fixtures and require an explicit `PASS`. Promote the boundary test into the project's permanent test suite. Run `typecheck`, `codebase-invariant-check` (when applicable), focused tests, and full suite checks when feasible. After all verification commands finish, remove only the round-owned `.temp_files/proof-driven-type-boundary-guard/<round-id>/` directory. Never delete `.temp_files/` wholesale or touch another process's artifacts.

### 5. Report and stop
Start with one honest outcome: `fixed-and-verified`, `fixed-verification-incomplete`, `no-proven-bug`, or `blocked`. Report:

1. Unsafe boundary/cast location, how malformed runtime data breached it, and affected files.
2. Proof command and pre-fix `FAIL` output.
3. Runtime guard and type narrowing applied.
4. Post-fix proof, `typecheck` status, permanent regression test path, and cleanup status.
5. Required skills loaded, and any that were unavailable.

Include the investigated scope, coverage gaps, and a short root-cause fingerprint (affected path + boundary input + enforced type contract) for deduplication in later rounds. Then stop this turn. Do not harden a second unrelated boundary in the same turn. When the user has configured multiple rounds, the application's next-round continuation is already authorized; follow it without asking for the same approval again.
